summary: A report on the February 1972 Data Management Working Group meeting. It summarizes talks on network applications, such as medical simulation and the MEDLINE system, then discussions of what the working group should do.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 316 reports on a meeting about sharing data across computer networks. Participants discussed real examples, problems with incompatible systems and steps toward a shared data service.

subtitle: Notes on the network data management working group's meeting

tldr.problem: The meeting explored how people could locate, describe and use data held by different network systems.
tldr.mechanism: Participants presented current applications and discussed shared languages, directories, conversion and access controls.
tldr.outcome: The group outlined a possible progression from routing file requests to broader interaction among local data systems.

today: RFC 316 records discussions and plans from a data management working group meeting. It does not define a finished network data management system.

sections.title: Examples of Network Data Use
sections.content:
The meeting included reports on medical simulation, the MEDLINE journal system, military command data and a network of computers at General Motors Research. These examples showed different ways that users might reach data or computing resources over a network.

Presenters also described the difficulty of using data held in systems with different organizations, hardware and local data management methods.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants described networks used for medical teaching, journal access, military data and engineering work. They also explained why systems could have trouble sharing information.

sections.title: A Staged Data Management Plan
sections.content:
The group discussed a progression of capabilities: route a file request to a named location; find data by name through a location catalog; share descriptions of data; convert data for the receiving system; translate file-access commands; retrieve selected pieces of data; and connect more generally to local data management systems.

The notes present these as possible stages, not as a completed implementation.
sections.plainLanguage: The group considered starting with simple file transfers and then adding catalogs, descriptions, conversion and access to parts of files. The final goal was to connect different local data systems.

sections.title: Experiments and Open Questions
sections.content:
The meeting discussed experiments that would translate a common network request into the language used at a particular site. It also considered where control and catalogs should be kept, how to describe different data structures, and how to protect important information.

Participants agreed that broader data access was worth pursuing, while noting that the choice of a common data language and the details of implementation required more study.
sections.plainLanguage: Researchers planned studies of how a shared request could work with different computers. They still needed to decide how to organize catalogs, describe data and protect it.
